manual/specs: PUMP P-201, centrifugal process pump, 3600 rpm (60 Hz), driven through a variable-frequency drive.
OEM Operation & Maintenance Manual, section 1: Specifications
Rated speed                 3600 rpm synchronous, ~3540 rpm at rated load (slip)
Thrust bearing (Tt)         normal operation: ambient + 44 C (+/- 2 C) at rated speed
Radial bearing (Tr)         normal operation: ambient + 38 C (+/- 2 C)
Bearing oil (To)            normal operation: ambient + 29 C (+/- 3 C, depends on cooling-water temperature)
Alarm                       Tt high at 72 C (10 min persistence)
Trip / damage limits        Tt 97 C, Tr 97 C, oil 77 C
Speed range on VFD          80-100 % of rated, ramp 10 %/min max
manual/thermal: All bearing and oil temperatures follow the pump-room ambient almost one for one in steady state:
a 5 C rise in room temperature raises Tt, Tr and oil by about 5 C each.
Bearing heat is generated by friction and scales with the friction coefficient times speed squared.
The thrust bearing has a thermal time constant of ~20 min; the oil sump ~25-60 min.
Heat from the bearings is rejected to the room and to the oil; the oil is cooled by a water-to-oil
cooler. Cooling-water temperature is not instrumented and causes slow oil-temperature swings of
- thrust bearing friction increase: Tt rises; oil rises slightly (about 0.2 C per C of Tt rise); Tr follows the oil.
- oil cooler fouling: oil rises first and most; Tr and Tt follow the oil (Tt rises ~0.45 C per C of oil rise).
- high room temperature: all three rise together with ambient, differences to ambient unchanged.
manual/troubleshooting: Section 7: Troubleshooting - high thrust bearing temperature (Tt alarm)
Possible causes, check in this order:
1. Room ambient high (ventilation fault, heat wave). Check ambient tag. Tt - ambient normal => no pump fault.
2. Oil cooling degraded (cooler fouling, low cooling-water flow). Check oil temperature vs ambient.
3. Instrument fault on the Tt RTD (drift, moisture in junction box, loose termination).
RTD drift is a slow, smooth offset and is NOT distinguishable from real heating on the reading alone.
Verify with a portable instrument, an RTD loop check, or the speed step test (section 8).
4. Thrust bearing distress (wear, lubrication film breakdown). Temperature rises progressively,
accelerating as damage progresses. Vibration at bearing defect frequencies may or may not be present.
Left unattended, bearing failure typically occurs within days of the alarm.
Do not replace the thrust bearing on a temperature alarm alone without ruling out causes 1-3.
manual/tests: Reduce speed to 90 % of rated for 45 min (flow drops ~15 %), then return to rated.
Bearing friction heat drops with speed squared, so a real bearing temperature responds.
For a thrust bearing at nominal friction, Tt drops by about 6 C over the 45 min
(the oil also cools ~2 C). The drop scales with the friction coefficient: a bearing with
20 % excess friction drops ~7 C, 40 % excess ~8 C.
Interpretation: a high Tt reading whose step response matches a NOMINAL bearing points to an
instrument offset; a larger-than-nominal drop points to increased bearing friction.
The test costs production (reduced flow for its duration). Deeper or longer steps give a larger,
easier-to-read response at a higher production cost.
8.2 Technician inspection (next shift, ~8 h lead time)
- Thrust bearing: portable IR reading on the bearing housing (reads ~2 C below the bearing, +/- 1 C)
and vibration route. Vibration indicates bearing distress in most but not all cases.
- RTD loop check: comparison with a reference probe, accuracy +/- 0.4 C.
- Oil cooler: visual inspection and water-side check; detects significant fouling in most cases.
manual/instrumentation: P201.TT_THRUST   thrust bearing RTD, C, 1-min, accuracy +/-0.25 C
P201.TT_OIL      bearing oil sump RTD, C

Historique des alarmes de temperature butee (Tt haute), flotte de 8 pompes, 2019-2026 :
- usure / degradation du roulement de butee : environ 30 % des cas
- derive de sonde RTD (souvent humidite dans la boite de jonction) : environ 30 %
- conditions ambiantes (canicule, ventilation du local en panne) : environ 25 %
2022-11 P-203 : alarme Tt, roulement remplace trop tard, bris en service, arret non planifie de 18 h.
2024-02 P-201 : alarme Tt, sonde RTD derivee de +7 C, remplacee. Roulement en bon etat.
2024-07 P-205 : alarmes Tt pendant canicule, aucun defaut, ventilation du local reparee.
2025-05 P-204 : huile chaude, refroidisseur encrasse (eau de riviere chargee), nettoye.
2025-09 P-201 : roulement remplace sur alarme Tt seule, sonde trouvee fautive apres coup.
remplacement roulement de butee en arret planifie ~28 k$ ; bris en service ~260 k$ (18 h d'arret)
remplacement sonde RTD ~1,5 k$ ; nettoyage refroidisseur ~6 k$ ; bris par surchauffe d'huile ~175 k$
visite technicien ~1,8 k$ (quart suivant) ; perte de production ~12 k$/h a debit nul

args.diagnosis: Degradation progressive du roulement de butee du P-201 (frottement accru, usure ou rupture du film lubrifiant). Ecart Tt-ambiant passe de 45 C a 54 C en 48 h (reference 44 C), avec acceleration depuis environ 4 h. Test de vitesse 90 % sur 45 min : Tt chute de 6,9 C, au-dessus de la reponse nominale (environ 6 C), donc frottement accru et non derive de sonde. Huile (+7 C) et palier radial (+6 C) montent seulement depuis environ 4 h : composante refroidisseur possible en second lieu. Ambiant exclu, car les ecarts a ambiant ont change pour les trois capteurs. Hausse legere cote butee deja notee au journal le 2026-10-07.
